    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("213.176.73.80", "95.164.53.100", "94.156.114.56", "150.241.105.82") or RemoteUrl has_any ("pasteflawwed.world")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["213.176.73.80", "95.164.53.100", "94.156.114.56", "150.241.105.82"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["pasteflawwed.world"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

HollowGraph DNS credential-refresh: IPv6 AAAA tunneling to cloudlanecdn[.]com AICommand & Control High
Hunts HollowGraph's out-of-band credential-refresh channel, which encodes new Entra ID tenant/client/secret/mailbox values inside IPv6 AAAA answers from the attacker-controlled cloudlanecdn[.]com (and typo variant cloudlanecdi[.]com). Each 16-byte AAAA record yields 14 usable payload bytes, so AAAA queries to these domains are the tunnel — not normal name resolution. Rationale: Pivots on the two article/Group-IB confirmed domains (cloudlanecdn.com plus typo variant cloudlanecdi.com) filtered to the AAAA record type Group-IB explicitly names as the tunnel encoding (14 payload bytes per 16-byte answer). Domain + AAAA is near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.group-ib.com/blog/hollowgraph-microsoft-365/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/hollowgraph-microsoft-calendars/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/hollowgraph-malware-hides-c2-and-stolen.html
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1572 T1132.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel enrichment platform or security scanner actively resolving the IOC domain from an analyst workstation
  • Passive-DNS or sinkhole appliance re-querying the domain
  • Malware-analysis sandbox VM on the corporate network detonating the sample
  • DNS logging/replay tooling replaying historical PCAP containing the domain
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the querying host and the process initiating the AAAA lookups (InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName); confirm it is not a TI/scanner appliance and that the process is a NativeAOT .NET binary or unsigned host. 2) Contain: block cloudlanecdn.com and cloudlanecdi.com at DNS/proxy, isolate the host, and treat any Entra ID app credentials on it as compromised — the tunnel refreshes tenantId/clientId/clientSecret. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for logAzure.txt writes and Microsoft Graph app-only sign-ins to the target mailbox; sweep the org for any other host resolving these domains.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["cloudlanecdn.com","cloudlanecdi.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["cloudlanecdn.com","cloudlanecdi.com"]);
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where QueryTypeName =~ "AAAA" or tostring(QueryType) == "28"
| where Name has_any (C2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, QueryTypeName, ResultCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HollowGraph config drop masquerading as a log file (logAzure.txt) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts creation or modification of logAzure.txt, HollowGraph's configuration file that masquerades as a routine Azure log but stores the Entra ID tenant ID, client ID, client secret, target mailbox, C2 domain and two RSA keys. The DNS tunnel rewrites this file on credential refresh, so writes to it are a direct implant artifact. Rationale: logAzure.txt is a Group-IB/BleepingComputer-named hunting IOC and is the single richest host artifact (holds the OAuth secret + RSA keys). Filename is specific enough for alerting; capturing the writing process gives immediate implant attribution. Cross-checked against: • https://www.group-ib.com/blog/hollowgraph-microsoft-365/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/hollowgraph-microsoft-calendars/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A homegrown or third-party Azure/deployment script that legitimately emits a log file literally named logAzure.txt
  • Developer diagnostic logging from an Azure SDK sample project
  • Backup/sync software copying a pre-existing file of that name into a new path
  • Security tooling restoring a quarantined copy of the artifact during IR
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msbuild.exe","func.exe","az.exe","dotnet.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the FolderPath and inspect the writing process (InitiatingProcessFileName) — a NativeAOT .NET host or unsigned/temp-path binary writing this file is malicious; a signed build/deploy tool in a dev repo is likely benign. 2) Contain: isolate the host and immediately revoke/rotate the Entra ID application client secret and any mailbox the file references, since its contents are exfiltration-grade credentials. 3) Hunt: correlate with AAAA queries to cloudlanecdn[.]com from the same host and with Graph app-only sign-ins to the referenced mailbox; sweep other endpoints for the same filename.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "logAzure.txt"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "logAzure.txt"
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Create","Modify")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HollowGraph implant execution by SHA256 (Cavern framework module) AIInstallation Medium
Alerting detection for the three Group-IB-published HollowGraph (Cavern framework) sample hashes across process creation, image load and file write. HollowGraph is a .NET NativeAOT DLL, so it can surface as a loaded module, a dropped file, or a directly executed image. Rationale: Three exact SHA256 values published in the article's IOC set and corroborated by Group-IB's report; hash matches are unambiguous. Union across image-load/process/file covers the NativeAOT-DLL delivery variants (loaded, dropped, or directly run). Cross-checked against: • https://www.group-ib.com/blog/hollowgraph-microsoft-365/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/hollowgraph-malware-hides-c2-and-stolen.html
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox or reverse-engineering VM detonating the sample intentionally
  • EDR/AV quarantine or sample-submission process copying the file
  • Threat-intel repository or YARA lab host holding the sample for research
  • Backup restore surfacing a previously-collected forensic copy
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hash hit is on a production host (not a sandbox/IR analyst VM) and capture the FolderPath, loading process and user context. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill/quarantine the module, and rotate the Entra ID app secret + affected mailbox credentials the implant would have loaded from logAzure.txt. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for logAzure.txt, AAAA queries to cloudlanecdn[.]com, and app-only Microsoft Graph calendar activity on the targeted mailbox; sweep the estate for the other two hashes.

 (DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (HollowGraphHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Kind="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),

 (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (HollowGraphHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Kind="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc

HollowGraph calendar dead-drop: app-driven M365 events with 'Event ID:' / 'Boss{..}ID{..}' subjects AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the covert calendar dead-drop in the M365 unified audit log: HollowGraph creates/reads Exchange calendar events whose subjects follow the SEND format 'Boss{..}ID{..}' (stolen data attachments) and the GET format 'Event ID: <7-char taskID>' (attacker instructions), scheduled far in the future (May 13, 2050). Detects both the exfil and command-fetch sides of the Microsoft Graph C2. Rationale: The two HollowGraph command subject formats ('Event ID: <7-char>' for GET, 'Boss{..}ID{..}' for SEND) plus the fixed May 13 2050 date are Group-IB-documented, highly specific strings unlikely to occur in legitimate calendaring. Captures ClientInfoString/AppId to expose the app-only Graph caller Group-IB recommends auditing. Cross-checked against: • https://www.group-ib.com/blog/hollowgraph-microsoft-365/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/hollowgraph-microsoft-calendars/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/hollowgraph-malware-hides-c2-and-stolen.html
ATT&CKT1567 T1102.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A ticketing/ITSM integration that syncs calendar holds titled 'Event ID: <number>'
  • Room-booking or automation bots creating far-future recurring placeholder events
  • Calendar-migration tooling bulk-creating events with system-generated subjects
  • A user genuinely naming a meeting 'Boss 1:1' (mitigated by the '{..}ID{..}' structure)
Suppression filter
| where Subject matches regex @"(?i)^(Event ID:\s*[A-Za-z0-9]{7}\b|Boss.*ID\{)"
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the matching events' ClientInfoString/ClientIP and the authenticating app (AppId/service principal) — app-only Graph access to a single mailbox creating 2050-dated events with these subjects is the implant, not a user. 2) Contain: revoke the OAuth application's client secret/consent, block it via Conditional Access, and purge the malicious calendar events (they carry RSA/AES-encrypted stolen files). 3) Hunt: enumerate every mailbox the same AppId touched, pull the event attachments for scoping of exfiltrated data, and correlate with logAzure.txt / cloudlanecdn[.]com activity on endpoints for that user.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("Create","Update")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has "Event ID:" or Raw has "Boss{" or Raw has "2050-05-13"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, Application, ActionType, ObjectName, Raw
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange" or RecordType in~ ("ExchangeItem","ExchangeItemGroup","ExchangeItemAggregated")
| where Operation in~ ("Create","Update")
| where Subject startswith "Event ID:" or Subject startswith "Boss"
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, MailboxOwnerUPN, UserId, ClientIP, ClientInfoString, ItemType, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
sourcetype="o365:management:activity" (Operation="Create" OR Operation="Update") (Subject="Event ID:*" OR Subject="Boss*")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(ClientIP) as ClientIP values(ClientInfoString) as ClientInfoString by MailboxOwnerUPN, Subject, Operation
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| sort - count

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.

Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain

ImDnsActivity

            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff") or SHA1 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff") or MD5 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff") or SHA1 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff") or MD5 in~ ("75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["75e51774b8f79e5f256eaae639635f911b3e744d4774fd6068dd980255621509", "f3f3006f8304788251b153d53b305322b8acab0c66ec816b8d9f101bcc851da3", "b3d0f6e4e3be395fd7cf9e8101c89963d77216578cbb117a6ac9bc3564485eff"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Exposed Server Reveals AI-Assisted Phishing Toolkit Behind WebDAV Malware Campaign

The Hacker News
2026-07-20 20 use cases 10 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A malware operator left its delivery server wide open, and Rapid7 pulled down the whole toolkit: 1,048 files spanning lure templates, filename-spoofing tests, execution experiments, droppers, builder notes, and two campaign chains. One was already live against Windows users in Mexico, delivering an infostealer through a fake government ID-lookup site over WebDAV. What makes it more than a

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] search-ms: URI opening a remote WebDAV share filtered to .scr payloads · [LLM] RTLO / double-extension executable masquerading as a CURP PDF report · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] WebDAV working-directory hijack: signed binary spawns child from remote share (CVE-2025-33053) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Exposed Server Reveals AI-Assisted Phishing Toolkit Behind WebDAV Malware Campai
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Signed Ubisoft-branded binary executing from a user-writable path (DlrtyGames DLL side-load) · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Known Simba Service WebDAV campaign C2 IPs, domains and payload hashes · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
WebDAV working-directory hijack: signed binary spawns child from remote share (CVE-2025-33053) AIExploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2025-33053 technique the operator reproduced: a .url shortcut launches a legitimate signed Windows binary (e.g. iediagcmd.exe) whose working directory points at an attacker WebDAV share, so a bare-filename helper like route.exe is loaded from the remote DavWWWRoot instead of System32. Detection keys on any process whose image path resolves to a WebDAV share (DavWWWRoot / @SSL@ crumbs), which is the article's core execution primitive. Rationale: Anchors on the exact WebDAV path markers (DavWWWRoot, @SSL@) that appear in the operator's recovered README example summerartcamp[.]net@ssl@443\DavWWWRoot\OSYxaOjr and in Check Point's original Stealth Falcon writeup of CVE-2025-33053 — any executable image resolving from a WebDAV share is anomalous. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/stealth-falcon-zero-day/ • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1574.008 T1204.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WebDAV-mounted document shares in enterprises that publish tools over SSL WebDAV
  • Sysinternals live.sysinternals.com WebDAV usage by admins running tools directly from the share
  • SharePoint/Office WebDAV drive redirection when opening Office binaries from a mapped SSL share
  • Backup or DMS agents that stage executables on a WebDAV endpoint
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "sysinternals" and DeviceName in (dynamic([])))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the parent process and command line — confirm a signed system binary (iediagcmd.exe, or one of the 59 candidate LOLBAS/.NET tools) launched a helper whose FolderPath is a remote DavWWWRoot/@SSL@ share; capture the WebDAV host and correlate to the C2 IOC list. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill the process tree, and block the WebDAV host at proxy/firewall; disable the WebClient service via GPO on at-risk fleets. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep for .url files referencing @SSL@/DavWWWRoot, WebClient service starts, and davclnt.dll reaching external hosts across the estate.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "DavWWWRoot" or FolderPath has "@SSL@"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has "DavWWWRoot" or NewProcessName has "@SSL@"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7d2f9a41-6c3e-4b7a-9f21-1a4e8c0d5b62

search-ms: URI opening a remote WebDAV share filtered to .scr payloads AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the delivery step where the gobf[.]mx CURP lookalike page's download button fired a search-ms: query that opened the operator's WebDAV share as an Explorer search filtered to .scr files. Detection keys on process command lines combining the search-ms: protocol handler with a remote WebDAV crumb, the article's specific initial-access mechanism. Rationale: The article explicitly states the download button fired a search-ms: query opening the WebDAV share filtered to .scr files; the search-ms:+WebDAV-crumb pairing is a high-fidelity, article-specific delivery artifact rarely seen in benign use. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/stealth-falcon-zero-day/
ATT&CKT1204.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Power users invoking saved Explorer searches (.search-ms) against internal file servers
  • Legitimate enterprise WebDAV document portals accessed via search connectors
  • IT scripts building search-ms federated search connectors for SharePoint
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Extract the remote host from the search-ms crumb and confirm whether the target extension filter is .scr/.exe; check browser history for gobf[.]mx or other CURP-lookalike domains immediately prior. Step 2 (contain): Block the WebDAV host and typosquat domain; quarantine any .scr downloaded from the share. Step 3 (hunt): Look for subsequent .scr execution, Inno Setup child processes, and injection into signed Qihoo 360 (360*.exe) processes on the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "search-ms:"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DavWWWRoot", "@SSL@", "crumb")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "search-ms:"
| where CommandLine has_any ("DavWWWRoot", "@SSL@", "crumb")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

RTLO / double-extension executable masquerading as a CURP PDF report AIDelivery High
Hunts the most-delivered lure: a .scr executable whose filename was flipped with a right-to-left override (U+202E) to read as a PDF, or padded with a double extension. Detection keys on RTLO characters and pdf/doc/jpg-to-scr/exe double extensions in file writes, the article's specific masquerading trick. Rationale: The article names the lure precisely: a .scr Inno Setup installer whose filename was RTLO-flipped to read as a PDF; U+202E plus doc-to-scr double extensions are near-zero-FP masquerading signals and match a single CURP lure that drove 97.7% of launch events.
ATT&CKT1036.002 T1036.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Rare legitimate localized filenames that contain bidirectional text control characters (Arabic/Hebrew document names)
  • Security tooling deliberately writing EICAR-style test files with double extensions
  • Archive extractors preserving mojibake filenames from foreign-language ZIPs
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Render the raw filename bytes to confirm a U+202E override or double extension, then hash the file and check against the six published payload SHA256s. Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file, isolate the host if executed, and block the delivery WebDAV host. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the writing process for search-ms delivery and look for the Inno Setup loader executing and hollowing into a signed Qihoo 360 process.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName matches regex @"\x{202E}" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(pdf|docx?|jpe?g|png)\s*\.(scr|exe)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"\x{202E}" or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(pdf|docx?|jpe?g|png)\s*\.(scr|exe)$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Signed Ubisoft-branded binary executing from a user-writable path (DlrtyGames DLL side-load) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the DlrtyGames campaign chain where a trojanized DLL is side-loaded through a signed Ubisoft binary to drop a modular .NET RAT. Detection keys on a process whose version-info company is Ubisoft running from a user-writable directory (AppData/Downloads/Temp/ProgramData/Public), the placement pattern required for DLL side-loading. Rationale: The article names a signed Ubisoft binary side-loading a trojanized DLL to drop a .NET RAT in the DlrtyGames directory; anchoring on the Ubisoft signer company plus user-writable execution path captures the staging step. Datadog/Falcon left empty because signer-company (VersionInfo) fields are Defender/ASIM-native and not carried on stock Sysmon/FDR process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ubisoft Connect / Uplay legitimate updater and game launchers that self-update into AppData
  • Portable Ubisoft game copies run from a user Downloads or Desktop folder
  • QA/dev machines running unpackaged Ubisoft builds from Temp
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("UbisoftConnect.exe", "UplayInstaller.exe", "upc.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Enumerate DLLs loaded by the Ubisoft binary and flag any DLL from the same user-writable folder (side-load target) or unsigned/mismatched-company DLLs; hash both binary and DLL against the published IOCs. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill the process, and block C2 addresses 77.110.127.205 / 23.94.252.228. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to .NET RAT behavior — outbound to the campaign C2 domains and persistence writes across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Ubisoft" or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Ubisoft"
| where FolderPath has_any ("AppData", "Downloads", "Temp", "ProgramData", "Public")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany has "Ubisoft"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("AppData", "Downloads", "Temp", "ProgramData", "Public")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessFileCompany
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Signed Ubisoft Binary Executing From User-Writable Path

Known Simba Service WebDAV campaign C2 IPs, domains and payload hashes AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on Rapid7-published indicators for both campaign chains: connections to the C2 IPs/domains or execution/write of any of the six .NET infostealer/RAT payload hashes. Straight IOC coverage to block first, per the article's guidance. Rationale: Uses the exact Rapid7-published C2 IPs (77.110.127.205, 23.94.252.228), campaign domains (gobf.mx, onedrive.cv, google.services.ug, summerartcamp.net) and six payload SHA256 hashes; these are confirmed indicators the article directs defenders to block first. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/rapid7/Rapid7-Labs
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scanners / sandboxes in your own estate deliberately resolving the C2 domains
  • Security researchers detonating the samples in an isolated VLAN that still ships EDR telemetry
  • Passive DNS or URL-reputation appliances pre-fetching the typosquat domain
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the connecting process and whether the source host is a sandbox/research VM vs a production endpoint; correlate to any preceding search-ms/WebDAV or RTLO .scr activity. Step 2 (contain): Block the IPs and domains at egress and quarantine any host matching a payload hash. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep for the WebDAV hijack, RTLO lures, and Ubisoft side-load UCs on any host that touched the C2, and check for Qihoo 360 process hollowing.
let C2Ips = dynamic(["77.110.127.205", "23.94.252.228"]);
let C2Domains = dynamic(["gobf.mx", "onedrive.cv", "google.services.ug", "summerartcamp.net"]);
let Payloads = dynamic(["04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2Ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Account = InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator = strcat(RemoteIP, " ", RemoteUrl), Proc = InitiatingProcessFileName, Detail = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in (Payloads)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Account = InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator = SHA256, Proc = InitiatingProcessFileName, Detail = FolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)

    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation

            - '\psexesvc.exe'

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923") or SHA1 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923") or MD5 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923") or SHA1 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923") or MD5 in~ ("04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["04a8018191f2e9e76072d072a933371d9d669a42de2b2a087541cd3a653b0ba7", "e8be17a7fbef48b45f1e958b3ae5ebdfcad58808969982c431a905eefcae5268", "449d1121fa275879af22a20407aa7253ac750ac8fa7ff5691101752600d645df", "a88f5ee748e60f889d046718bfe3ddcf1c5f3cba2001cad587e8953a76bf7aa9", "51a02eccdcae0483c7cbb9796738eee6c2a13b740d30e5417cda09bf418ea93b", "82e67735cf822db8f2f759e742e5bf8c54fdbd01a4170619b9e0916e1b3f5923"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Exposed Server Reveals AI-Assisted Phishing Toolkit Behind WebDAV Malware Campai Exploitation High

Critical

HollowGraph Malware Hides C2 and Stolen Files in Microsoft 365 Events Dated 2050

The Hacker News
2026-07-20 17 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A newly discovered espionage implant has been using a hijacked Microsoft 365 calendar as its command channel, planting operator instructions and smuggling out stolen files as attachments on calendar events dated to the year 2050. Group-IB, which named the malware HollowGraph, says the approach moves tasking and stolen data through legitimate Microsoft Graph API traffic, so the activity looks
